newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian court rejects Chinese refugee bid.
newsitem.headline: Australian court rejects Chinese refugee bid.

text.p: Australia's highest appeal court on Monday rejected China's one-child policy as grounds for refugee status in a move that could affect hundreds of Chinese seeking refuge in Australia.
The High Court dismissed an asylum bid by a Chinese couple who said they had a well-founded fear of being forcibly sterilised if returned to China, a court official told Reuters.
In a 3-2 majority, the court said the couple, identified only as A and B, could not prove they faced persecution as members of "a particular social group" under international conventions on refugees.
The couple arrived by boat in December, 1993. The woman gave birth soon after their arrival and they applied to the Immigration Department for refugee status.
Their original application was approved by the Refugee Review Tribunal and was confirmed by the Federal Court when challenged by the government.
But that decision was overturned by the full bench of the Federal Court and the couple appealed to the High Court.

Their lawyer, outside the court, appealed to Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock to allow the couple and their child to stay in Australia on humanitarian grounds, the domestic news agency Australian Associated Press reported.
Monday's court decision sets a precedent for scores of other Chinese families seeking asylum on the same grounds.

China, which has 1.2 billion people, allows each couple to have only one child under a strict birth control policy launched in 1979. Urban families breaking the rule officially face fines but human rights groups have accused China of using forced abortions and sterilisations to check population growth.
